map.name: Defense Challenge
map.testedVersion: Selected-artifact v1.1.3 source/package conservation audit; SHA-256 14a0dcb7354a69edb9d83c0f8c1e9fd160c29238011aeb817bcdaf31c098fced. Findings are promoted only from the selected Defense artifact plus current approved Defense design requirements; sibling maps and historical reports are search pressure, not proof.

bugs.title: Levels 5–9 can resolve OPPOSITE into a direction that is not active for the level
bugs.problem: Dynamic OPPOSITE targeting transforms the previous direction by compass opposite without revalidating the result against the level's active directions.
bugs.expected: Every resolved spawn direction remains inside the current level's declared direction domain.
bugs.observed: Levels 5–6 declare north/east and Levels 7–9 declare north/east/west, but OPPOSITE(north) resolves south; South routes are configured and materialized even though South is not active until Level 10.
reproduction: Start Defense Challenge on Level 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 with the declared active fronts visible for that level.
Reach a wave entry that uses OPPOSITE after the previous dynamic target resolves to North.
Observe which logical spawn route is selected for the OPPOSITE entry.
Confirm whether South is selected even though South is not declared active until Level 10.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The resulting South target is routable; no post-transform domain guard was found.

relevantCode.reason: Levels 5–9 restricted direction sets and OPPOSITE entries.

bugs.suggestedFix: Validate every transformed direction against levelConfig.directions and choose a deterministic valid fallback when the opposite front is inactive.
mustPreserve: South dual-route behavior from Level 10 onward
bugs.whyThisIsBug: Levels 5–9 explicitly restrict which fronts are active. OPPOSITE is applied after that level-domain selection but its result is not checked against the same active-direction list, so the runtime can use a front that the current level configuration did not enable.
bugs.impact: Players can be attacked from South before South is introduced by the level progression. Defensive positioning, block placement, team coverage, and encounter difficulty can therefore differ from the authored Level 5–9 front layout.

bugs.title: Reload does not faithfully restore deferred wave timing and delayed spawn groups
bugs.problem: Persisted session state records launched-wave progress but does not fully persist/reconstruct remaining inter-wave and intra-wave deferred work.
bugs.expected: Reload preserves the same pending timing and delayed spawn groups that existed immediately before reload.
bugs.observed: Recovery resumes from lastLaunchedWaveIndex without using currentWaveElapsedTicks as remaining-delay authority. Level 15 Wave 3 is marked launched before its +10-second East/West group of six NPCs materializes, so reload in that window can lose the in-memory delayed group.
reproduction: Start a level with a pending delayed wave or delayed spawn group and note the remaining delay.
Reload or recover the persisted Defense session before the pending delay expires.
Observe the timing and composition of the next resumed wave or group.
For Level 15 Wave 3, reload during the 10-second delay before the East/West six-NPC group and confirm whether that delayed group is reconstructed.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Wave-index persistence is not sufficient to reconstruct all scheduled work.
bugs.suggestedFix: Persist a reconstructable pending-wave timeline including remaining delays for intra-wave delayed groups.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: A persisted active session must resume the same outstanding encounter work, not merely remember which wave index was last launched. The current recovery state cannot reconstruct remaining delays or delayed sub-groups, so reload changes the encounter that was in progress.
bugs.impact: After reload, a pending wave can arrive at the wrong time, and Level 15 can permanently omit the delayed East/West group of six NPCs. This changes combat pressure and can make the resumed run easier or structurally different from the pre-reload run.

bugs.title: Shears special enemy resolves to ordinary Tier 2 behavior with no special-behavior consumer
bugs.problem: The manifest defines SHEARS as a distinct gameplay type, but runtime maps it to Tier 2 militia and only adds shears_carrier.
bugs.expected: A distinct SHEARS gameplay type has an authoritative behavior consumer differentiating it from ordinary Tier 2 militia.
bugs.observed: Across the selected artifact, shears_carrier appears only where the tag is added; no script, entity, controller, or behavior consumer reads it.
reproduction: Reach a level that spawns the SHEARS special enemy.
Place the same valid defensive obstruction in the Shears path and in an ordinary Tier 2 militia path.
Compare the Shears enemy block interaction and combat behavior with ordinary Tier 2 militia.
Confirm whether any distinct Shears behavior is observable.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The special identity survives as metadata but not as behavior.

relevantCode.reason: SHEARS materialization and sole shears_carrier occurrence.

bugs.suggestedFix: Give SHEARS one explicit behavior owner or remove the distinct type if ordinary Tier 2 behavior is intended.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: SHEARS is authored as a distinct enemy type in the Defense wave manifest, but its only runtime distinction is a shears_carrier tag that nothing in the selected artifact consumes. A named special enemy therefore has no implemented behavior that makes the special type meaningful.
bugs.impact: A wave that is configured to introduce a Shears-specific threat behaves like an ordinary Tier 2 militia encounter. Players do not receive the intended mechanical variation, and level difficulty/composition no longer matches the authored special-enemy identity.

bugs.title: Configured captureZone is not the authoritative flag-capture boundary
bugs.problem: Arena configuration describes captureZone as hostile flag detection, while FlagService uses it for warning coverage and a separate hard-coded radius for defeat.
bugs.expected: Warning and defeat boundaries have one explicit non-conflicting authority whose naming matches runtime behavior.
bugs.observed: captureZone is configured/offset per arena, but actual defeat uses horizontal radius 1.3 and vertical radius 1.5.
reproduction: Run a Defense level with a hostile approaching the configured flag captureZone.
Observe the hostile while it is inside the configured captureZone but outside the hard-coded 1.3-block horizontal defeat radius.
Confirm whether warning state and defeat state use different boundaries.
Repeat near the 1.3-block boundary to identify the actual defeat trigger.
bugs.aiAnalysis: This is an internal authority mismatch, not a claim that 1.3 itself is the wrong gameplay value.

relevantCode.reason: Warning-zone derivation and hard-coded defeat radius.

bugs.suggestedFix: Choose one capture authority and rename/separate warning configuration if the hard-coded defeat radius is canonical.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The arena configuration presents captureZone as the flag-detection boundary, but runtime defeat is decided by a separate hard-coded 1.3 horizontal / 1.5 vertical radius. Two different authorities therefore describe the same objective boundary.
bugs.impact: Warning and defeat behavior can be reasoned about from different spatial rules. Designers and developers can tune captureZone without changing the actual defeat trigger, creating misleading configuration and making flag-balance changes unreliable.

bugs.title: Defense does not implement the approved crafting-UI disablement
bugs.problem: Approved Defense design requires crafting UI unavailable during gameplay, but no crafting-screen UI override or equivalent owner exists.
bugs.expected: Crafting UI is unavailable throughout Defense gameplay while intended inventory, kit and shop interactions remain available.
bugs.observed: Selected RP contains HUD/information UI only. BP recipe overrides for stick/crafting table are not UI-level disablement.
reproduction: Start Defense Challenge and enter normal gameplay with inventory access.
Open the inventory and crafting interface.
Confirm whether the crafting UI remains available.
Verify that intended inventory, kit, and shop surfaces remain otherwise usable.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Current approved Defense requirement is not implemented in the selected artifact.

relevantCode.reason: Recipe overrides do not disable crafting UI.

bugs.suggestedFix: Implement one explicit Defense crafting-availability owner at UI/capability level.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The approved Defense requirement is to disable the crafting UI itself during gameplay. The selected artifact only changes specific recipes and does not remove or disable the crafting interface, so the implemented behavior does not satisfy the approved UI rule.
bugs.impact: Players can still access a gameplay surface that is supposed to be unavailable. This makes the interaction rules inconsistent and leaves crafting visible even when individual recipes have been restricted.

bugs.title: Retry configuration declares full-level restart while runtime uses remaining-NPC checkpoint recovery
bugs.problem: marathonConfig.retryMode is full_level_restart, but it is not consumed as a behavior branch; retryLevel() preserves killed NPC IDs and resumes from the first incomplete wave.
bugs.expected: Declared retry mode and implemented retry behavior describe the same policy.
bugs.observed: retryMode is effectively logging metadata while remaining-NPC checkpoint behavior is hard-coded.
reproduction: Start a Defense level and defeat only part of the configured NPC population.
Trigger a level failure that enters retry.
Observe which enemies and wave state are restored for the retry.
Confirm that already-killed configured NPCs remain preserved and retry resumes remaining NPCs rather than performing a full-level restart.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The runtime checkpoint path is coherent; the mismatch is stale configuration.
bugs.suggestedFix: Make remaining_npc_checkpoint canonical and consumed, or remove the unused mode abstraction.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The canonical configuration declares full_level_restart, while the actual retry implementation preserves killed NPCs and resumes remaining encounter state. The declared mode is not the behavior the game executes.
bugs.impact: Developers reading or changing retryMode can reasonably expect a full restart but receive checkpoint-style recovery instead. Future balancing, fixes, or tooling can make incorrect decisions because configuration and runtime semantics disagree.

bugs.title: Defense result records identify v1.1.3 as v1.1.0
bugs.problem: Machine-readable level/run record IDs use stale release provenance.
bugs.expected: World/pack metadata and result persistence consume one canonical version and report 1.1.3.
bugs.observed: DEFENSE_RECORD_VERSION is hard-coded to 1.1.0 and embedded in level and run record IDs.
reproduction: Complete or terminate a Defense run so level and run result records are persisted.
Inspect the generated Defense level and run record IDs.
Compare the version segment in those IDs with the selected world, BP, and RP version 1.1.3.
Confirm whether persisted record provenance still reports 1.1.0.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Selected world/BP/RP are v1.1.3 while score persistence carries the older literal.
bugs.suggestedFix: Consume one canonical release/version owner for persisted result provenance.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The selected world, behavior pack, and resource pack are v1.1.3, but persisted Defense result IDs still identify the run as v1.1.0. Result provenance therefore does not match the artifact that produced it.
bugs.impact: Automated analysis, debugging, comparison, and historical result tracking can attribute v1.1.3 gameplay data to the wrong release. This weakens version traceability and can cause results from different builds to be grouped incorrectly.
